Reverse a string by its characters as a reader sees them, so combining marks stay on their letters.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/reverse-string) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: reverse_string.nomi
//# Reverses a string.

/// Reverses `text` by grapheme, so a combining mark stays on its letter.
pub fn reverse(text: String) -> String {
    String.reverse(text)
}

// FILE: reverse_string_test.nomi
import reverse_string.reverse

test "reverses strings" {
    cases = [
        #("an empty string", "", ""),
        #("a word", "robot", "tobor"),
        #("a capitalized word", "Ramen", "nemaR"),
        #("a sentence with punctuation", "I'm hungry!", "!yrgnuh m'I"),
        #("a palindrome", "racecar", "racecar"),
        #("an even-sized word", "drawer", "reward"),
        #("wide characters", "子猫", "猫子"),
        #("grapheme cluster with pre-combined form", "Würstchenstand", "dnatsnehctsrüW"),
        #("grapheme clusters", "ผู้เขียนโปรแกรม", "มรกแรปโนยขีเผู้"),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, expected), description {
        assert reverse(text) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The solution is `String.reverse`, which already reverses by grapheme, so
  the two grapheme-cluster cases pass with no extra work. A hand-written
  `Iter.reverse(text) |> String.join()` does the same thing and would only
  restate the stdlib.
